subject: Discovery recap: embeddings / reranking for BrightCart
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@brightcart.com>, Priya Shah <priya@brightcart.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap: embeddings / reranking for BrightCart

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the clear context on your use case. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points
- Relevance drift at scale: you’re seeing degraded search/recommendation relevance as catalog and behavioral signals grow.
- Latency/cost tradeoff: current rerank step is expensive and exceeds latency targets under peak load.
- Ops burden: engineering is spending a lot of time tuning hybrid pipelines and handling cold-starts for new items.

Current stack (what you described)
- Metadata, catalog: Postgres/Cloud SQL for item metadata and product graph.
- Vector index: Redis Vector (primary) for low-latency lookup; FAISS offline indexing for nightly batch rerank.
- Serving: Python microservice that does retrieval -> candidates -> neural rerank.

Workload characteristics (your estimates)
- Index size: ~25M vectors (1536-d), growing ~2–3M / mo.
- Query traffic: baseline 40–60 QPS, peak ~120 QPS during promo spikes.
- Query pattern: mix of single-query low-latency (interactive search) and batched rerank jobs (hourly/nearline batches of 10k–100k).
- Latency target: P95 end-to-end < 50ms for interactive queries (rerank+retrieve); cost target ~$0.005 per query (targeting overall infra + model cost).

Success criteria (pilot)
- Match or improve relevance over current rerank model on same eval set.
- Meet P95 latency target for interactive queries at realistic QPS (we’ll define traffic profile).
- Demonstrate predictable cost and autoscaling behavior during spikes.

Proposed next steps
1) Share a brief pilot scope and a small sample (5–10k anonymized vectors + metadata) so we can run a quick baseline. Attachment: pilot-scope.pdf.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineers to discuss indexing, sharding, and fallback policies (suggested attendees: Neha and Rishi from our side).
3) Security/compliance: you mentioned a quick SOC2 questionnaire — I’ll attach a copy of our standard questionnaire and we can triage gaps.

If that looks right, I’ll send a calendar invite for the tech deep-dive and spin up a pilot config we can run against your sample.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(650) 555-0191

Attachments: pilot-scope.pdf
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@brightcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: embeddings / reranking for BrightCart

Thanks Marissa — that summary is spot-on. A few clarifications from our side:

- Index details: the 25M number is for product catalog vectors; we also maintain ~5M session/behavior vectors separately (we'd be open to consolidating for the pilot). Vectors are 1536-d, produced by a mix of in-house encoders and OpenAI embeddings.
- Vector DB: Redis Vector (hosted) is our primary low-latency store. FAISS runs in our batch pipelines for large reranks and A/B experiments. We’ve also evaluated Milvus but stuck with Redis for now due to ops familiarity.
- Query mix: interactive search is ~70% of traffic (single queries w/ rerank); the other 30% are batched scoring jobs (10k–50k at a time).
- Cost target: the $0.005/query is a blended target (we’re flexible if you break down infra vs model costs).

We can share a sanitized sample (5k product vectors + metadata) — Priya will prep. Also +1 on a tech call. Would Tuesday 3/9 at 10am PT work for your eng team?

Alex
Head of Search
BrightCart
alex@brightcart.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@brightcart.com>, Priya Shah <priya@brightcart.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T16:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: embeddings / reranking for BrightCart

Thanks Alex — great context and helpful numbers. 3/9 10am PT works for our engineering leads; I’ll send a calendar invite to lock that.

For the tech deep-dive agenda we’ll propose:
- Traffic profile and realistic QPS for the pilot
- Index sharding strategy (hot/cold split and prefix/KV caching)
- Vector DB compatibility and migration options (Redis vs Milvus vs FAISS snapshot workflows)
- Quantization/precision options to meet cost targets (e.g., 8-bit/4-bit and impact on accuracy)
- Canary plan for progressive rollout and fallback policies

Pilot approach (recommended):
- Phase 1: run 5M-vector pilot in a controlled environment to validate P95 latency and relevance.
- Phase 2: scale to 25M and simulate peak traffic (120 QPS) with autoscaling policy.

I’m attaching a short security questionnaire we commonly use — if you can return that, our security team will prioritize. Attachment: security-questionnaire.xlsx

Next actions I’ll take:
- Send invite for 3/9 10am PT and include Neha and Rishi.
- Provision a pilot config and a sample evaluation harness.

Looking forward —
Marissa

Attachments: security-questionnaire.xlsx
From: Priya Shah <priya@brightcart.com>

Marissa — thanks, that plan looks good. We’ll get the sanitized sample and the completed security questionnaire to you by end of day Monday.

One ask from procurement/security: can you share a copy of your SOC2 attestation or point us to where we can get that? Also, is there a standard NDA/PO template you use for pilots?

Alex and I will be on the 3/9 call. Thanks for looping in Neha and Rishi.

— Priya
